role.altitude: The judge keeps hearing, ruling, deciding sentences, instructing and writing the reasoning; assembling records and guidelines, checking procedural dates, retyping parties and procedural history and redacting names by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A judge whose files and decision shells are ready, so the time goes to hearing and reasoning.

tasks.short: Review the criminal record, reports and sentencing guidelines, hear sentencing arguments, decide and pronounce the sentence for defendants in criminal cases according to applicable statutes.

steps.what: Judge reviews the criminal record, probation report and sentencing guidelines
Judge hears sentencing arguments from prosecution and defence
Judge decides the sentence according to applicable statutes
Judge pronounces and explains the sentence in court

tasks.design: The digital case file opens on the criminal record extract, probation and expert reports, and the court's own sentencing guideline points for the offence, instead of the judge searching the file and the guideline booklet. No software suggests a sentence. Hearing, deciding and pronouncing stay with the judge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records, reports and guidelines sat in different places.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital case files with structured views.
tasks.still_hard: Cases where reports arrive at the last minute.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a defendant's remorse heard in court.

evidence.claim: AI used by a judicial authority to apply law to facts is high-risk, so no software suggests sentences here.
The Dutch judiciary targets low-risk AI uses and none in high-risk processes for now.

assumptions: Boundary: sentencing; reading pleadings (task 5647) and writing decisions (task 5653) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: record extracts and reports added to the digital case file by court staff.
Hearing, deciding and pronouncing keep their full time.
unknowns: How complete digital case files are.
research_questions: Does preparation per sentencing hearing fall?

incremental.description: Judge reports missing documents in the case file view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: paper-heavy files; high: complete digital files.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Follow the hearing, check procedural deadlines and steps in the case file, and intervene and rule on procedural issues to monitor proceedings so all applicable rules and procedures are followed.

steps.what: Judge follows the hearing and monitors that applicable rules and procedures are followed
Judge checks procedural deadlines and steps in the case file
Judge intervenes and rules on procedural issues

tasks.design: The case system shows a procedural timeline with filing dates, served documents and statutory deadlines, and flags any missed step, instead of the judge leafing back through the file. Following the hearing and ruling stay fully with the judge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedural history had to be traced through the file.
tasks.still_hard: Procedural questions raised unexpectedly in court.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a tense hearing fair to both sides.

reach.learn: Whether missed steps are caught before the hearing.

evidence.claim: A case records app with date rules and notifications handles deadlines without a model.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring proceedings; interpreting and setting procedural rules (task 5648) is a sibling task.
Following the hearing and ruling keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether all filings are dated in the case system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: simple cases; high: long cases with many filings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare instructions on applicable law, instruct juries and direct them to deduce the facts from the evidence presented, answer their questions, and hear their verdicts.

steps.what: Judge prepares the instructions on applicable laws
Judge instructs the jury and directs it to deduce the facts from the evidence
Judge answers the jury's questions during deliberation

tasks.design: Instructions start from the court's library of standard instructions per offence and element, which the judge adapts to the case, instead of writing them anew. No software applies the law to the facts. Instructing, answering questions and hearing the verdict stay with the judge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were assembled from earlier cases by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining reasonable doubt so jurors understand it.

evidence.claim: Templates and clause libraries come first in drafting; a person signs.
The Netherlands has no jury trials, so this task applies only where juries sit.

assumptions: Boundary: instructing juries; ruling on admissibility (task 5645) is a sibling task.
Instructing, answering and hearing the verdict keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of jury trials per year where this applies.
research_questions: Do jurors ask fewer clarifying questions?

incremental.description: Judge keeps the instruction library current after law changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual offences; high: common offences with standard instructions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up the decision with parties and procedural history, write findings and reasoning, add the operative part and appeal-rights text, check and sign the final decision, and check redactions for publication to write decisions on cases.

steps.what: Judge sets up the decision: parties, procedural history and claims
Judge writes the findings of fact and reasoning of decisions on cases
Judge adds the operative part and the appeal-rights text
Judge checks and signs the final decision
Judge checks the redactions of names and personal details for publication

loop.output: A publication version with names, addresses and other identifying details marked for replacement.
loop.check: The judge or clerk reviews every proposed redaction and searches for missed names of parties and witnesses.
loop.stop: Unclear passages are redacted by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Names and identifying details appear in many forms in free text.

tasks.design: The decision template fills parties, representatives, procedural history and claims from the case system, instead of the judge retyping them. Findings and reasoning are written by the judge; no model drafts them. The operative part uses standard wording and the fixed appeal-rights text per case type. After signing, a pseudonymisation step marks names and identifying details for the publication version, and the judge or clerk checks every mark.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard parts were retyped and redaction was done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Decision templates fed by the case system and pseudonymisation tools.
tasks.still_hard: Decisions where identifying details are part of the reasoning.
tasks.human_edge: Writing reasoning the losing party can accept as fair.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping and redacting; reasoning stays.

evidence.claim: The Dutch judiciary targets low-risk AI uses such as pseudonymising rulings and none in high-risk processes for now.
AI used by a judicial authority to apply law to facts is high-risk.
A judge used a chatbot to set the lifespan of solar panels in a ruling.

assumptions: Boundary: writing decisions; researching legal issues and writing opinions (task 5651) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: parties and procedural steps registered in the case system by court staff.
Reasoning and signing keep their full time.
research_questions: Does time from hearing to decision fall?

incremental.description: Judge reports template errors and missed redactions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short decisions; high: long decisions with many parties and publication.
